An analysis of a smoke alarm giveaway program in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, was published in the journal Injury Prevention in 2001, highlighting its outcomes and implications for public safety. 2. Jutkowitz et al. (2012) evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a home-based intervention designed to assist functionally vulnerable older adults in aging in place, as detailed in the Journal of Aging Research. 3. Salkeld et al. (2000) assessed the cost-effectiveness of a home hazard reduction program aimed at reducing falls among older individuals, with findings published in the Australia & New Zealand Journal of Public Health. 4. The World Health Organization (WHO) published comprehensive housing and health guidelines in 2018, addressing the intersection of living environments and public health. 5. Church et al. (2012) examined the cost-effectiveness of falls prevention interventions for older Australians living in the community, as reported in the Australia & New Zealand Journal of Public Health. 6. Frick et al. (2010) analyzed the cost-effectiveness of fall prevention programs that reduce fall-related hip fractures in older adults, with results published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society. 7. Ling et al. (2008) explored the cost-benefit considerations of preventing elderly falls through environmental modifications in homes in Hana, Maui, as documented in the Hawaii Medical Journal. 8. Kochera (2002) conducted an analysis of the costs, incidence, and potential savings associated with home modifications to prevent falls among older adults, published by the AARP Public Policy Institute. 9. The WHO's International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (2002) established a standardized framework for understanding and addressing disability and health-related challenges. 10. The World Report on Disability (2011) by the WHO provided a global perspective on the prevalence and impact of disability, emphasizing the need for inclusive policies. 11. The United Nations' World Population Ageing 2015 report highlighted demographic trends and their implications for aging populations worldwide. 12. The Centre on Housing Rights and Evictions (COHRE) (2004) provided commentary on the draft text of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, emphasizing the need for adequate housing and water access. 13. The Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (2006) was adopted by the United Nations to promote and protect the rights and dignity of individuals with disabilities. 14. Saville-Smith and Saville (2012) proposed practical approaches to encourage industry adoption of accessible housing designs in New Zealand, as outlined in a report for the Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment. 15. Ubani et al. (2013) investigated the accessibility and housing needs of paraplegics in Enugu City, Nigeria, as published in Civil and Environmental Research. 16. Smith et al. (2008) discussed the implications of aging and disability for the housing industry and policy in the United States, as reported in the Journal of the American Planning Association. 17. Close et al. (1999) conducted the Prevention of Falls in the Elderly Trial (PROFET), a randomized controlled trial published in The Lancet, to evaluate fall prevention strategies. 18. Whiteford (2000) addressed the global challenge of occupational deprivation in the new millennium, as discussed in the British Journal of Occupational Therapy. 19. Stanley et al. (2012) examined the implications of population aging, disability, and housing accessibility for sub-national areas in the United States, as published in Housing Studies. 20. Gitlin et al. (2014) identified factors influencing the quality of life for individuals with dementia living at home, focusing on the role of the home environment, caregivers, and patient characteristics, as reported in the American Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry. 21. Petersson et al. (2008) evaluated the impact of home modification services on daily life abilities for people aging with disabilities, as published in the Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine. 22. Gitlin et al. (2006) reported preliminary findings on the effect of in-home occupational and physical therapy interventions in reducing mortality among functionally vulnerable older adults, as detailed in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society. 23. Stineman et al. (2007) conducted a population-based study on home accessibility features and their impact on activities of daily living, with clinical and policy implications, as published in Disability & Rehabilitation. 24. Brunnström et al. (2004) examined the effects of lighting adaptations on quality of life for individuals with low vision, as reported in Ophthalmic & Physiological Optics. 25. Fänge and Iwarsson (2005) explored changes in housing accessibility and usability during the housing adaptation process, as published in Occupational Therapy International. 26. 27. Edgren et al. (2017) evaluated the effects of a home-based physical rehabilitation program on physical disability after hip fractures in a randomized controlled trial, as reported in the Journal of the American Medical Directors Association. 28. Tongsiri et al. (2017) assessed the modification of homes for individuals with physical disabilities in Thailand, as published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 29. Slaug et al. (2017) analyzed the short-term costs and long-term benefits of improved housing accessibility for older people in Sweden and Germany, as reported in the International Journal of Environmental Research & Public Health. 30. Tchalla et al. (2012) evaluated the efficacy of simple home-based technologies combined with a monitoring assistive center in reducing falls among frail elderly populations, as part of the Esoppe study, published in the Archives of Gerontology & Geriatrics.
